result.text:
### Q1
No. The JSON file store (data/store.json) stays, because ops backs it up nightly with an rsync job that diffs plain-text files, and a binary SQLite file would break their backup checks. Slowness is fixed by debouncing writes (200 ms) in src/store.ts, plus flush() on shutdown.
### Q2
Yes, src/legacy/. It is vendored from the old logistics monolith, and the platform team's sync job overwrites the folder every Monday, so any changes would be silently lost. Separately, docs/erp-api.md is owned by the ERP team and must not be edited.
### Q3
It goes in a top-level `sig` field in the JSON body, as HMAC-SHA256 hex over the body without `sig`. Before that I implemented an X-Signature header, and the ERP rejected every request as unsigned because their API gateway strips all custom X- headers. Header signing must not be reintroduced.
### Q4
Port 9911, since the October infra move. docs/erp-api.md and the README still say 8080, which is outdated.
### Q5
Any new user-facing error `message` must be in German, because warehouse staff see them verbatim. The `code` stays in English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.
### Q6
Austrian public holidays for 2026 and 2027 are in a hardcoded list in src/services/holidays.ts, which the ETA calculation uses. It's hardcoded because the warehouse deployment has no outbound internet, so it has to work fully offline.
### Q7
No. The user tried batching in September 2026, and the ERP answers 422 to any array payload. It accepts only a single event object per request, so batching must not be built.
### Q8
No new npm dependencies, not even dev deps. Each new package needs a security review that takes about 6 weeks.
### Q9
Yes. I memoized calculateEta, and QA then saw stale ETAs in GET /shipments after new events such as exceptions, because the cache wasn't invalidated and a proper cache key got messy. It was reverted at the user's request. Caching ETAs is a dead end. Paginating the list endpoint later is the planned alternative.
### Q10
There are at most 3 attempts in total, with a fixed 30 s delay and no exponential backoff. The ERP dedups by event_id only within a 2-minute window, so all attempts must land within 2 minutes or duplicates are created. Only network errors and 5xx responses are retried, and the delay must be injectable for tests.
### Q11
Never log a recipient's name, address or phone number, for GDPR reasons (the DPO flagged it in last month's audit). Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are fine to log.
### Q12
Yes, "emits webhook on delivered" in test/events.test.ts. It fails about 1 in 5 runs on CI because of a timer race in the fake notifier, tracked as OPS-412 and owned by the platform team. If it fails, rerun once and don't try to fix it.
### Q13
Only carrier ATP is validated, as UPU S10 including the check digit (algorithm in docs/carriers.md). All other carriers accept any non-empty value, because their formats change often and valid DHL numbers were wrongly rejected for 2 days last year.
### Q14
Hot reload is a future item and nothing needs building now. fs.watch never fires on staging, because the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and change events don't propagate. fs.watchFile (polling) worked when the user tried it last week.
### Q15
Yes, GET /shipments/:id. Its response must stay byte-for-byte the same shape, with no fields added or removed, because mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields. The next mobile release is in January. `eta` goes only on GET /shipments list items, added in the list route, not in the shared shipmentToApi.
